summary: In Greek mythology, Clonius (Ancient Greek Κλονίος) is one of the five Boeotian captains in Homer's Catalogue of Ships. Parentage varies — Alegenor; Alector and Acteis; or Lacritus and Cleobule (then brother of Leitus). He falls to Agenor, Antenor's son, in the fighting before Troy.
etymology: Ancient Greek Κλονίος (Kloníos), from κλόνος — "turmoil, battle-din."
cultCenters: Boeotia (Hyria, Aulis and the Boeotian towns)

sections.heading: Boeotian captain at Troy
paragraphs: Homer (Iliad 2.494–510) lists Clonius among the leaders of the Boeotian fifty ships. Hyginus (Fabulae 97, 114) makes him son of Lacritus and Cleobule and brother of Leitus; other authorities give Alegenor or Alector and Acteis. In Iliad 15 he is killed by Agenor.
Wikipedia's Clonius page also lists an illegitimate son of Priam, two Aeneid companions, and a Theban defender against the Seven — none of which is this Boeotian captain.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id clonius is the Homeric Boeotian leader alone. Cleobule his Hyginian mother is cleobule-boeotian, distinct from other Cleobules.
